stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: An LC tank loses energy to $R$ every cycle. An amplifier injects energy back with a gain $-G$ that behaves like a $\textit{negative resistance}$. Slide $L$, $C$, and $G$. Push $G$ below, at, and above $R$. Watch the envelope decay, sustain, then grow to saturation.
stages.concept: The loop equation is $L\,\ddot{q} + (R - G)\,\dot{q} + q/C = 0$. When $G < R$ the effective damping is positive so the envelope decays; when $G > R$ the amplifier over-compensates and the envelope grows until it hits the saturation ceiling $\pm U_{sat}$. Only then is oscillation $\textit{sustained}$, at the natural period $T_0 = 2\pi\sqrt{L\,C}$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Hit the orange crosshair: at $t^{*}$ the trace must reach the saturation ceiling $+U_{sat}$. Tune $L$ and $C$ to lock the period to $t^{*}$, and push $G$ above $R$ so the envelope grows and locks at $U_{sat}$.
stages.concept: The period condition is $T_0 = 2\pi\sqrt{L\,C} = t^{*}$. The saturation condition is $G > R$: the amplifier must inject more than the loop dissipates. Both conditions must hold — same product $L\,C$ works for many pairs.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Only the target curve is drawn. Read $T^{*}$ from peak-to-peak on the target, compute $L\,C = (T^{*}/2\pi)^{2}$ on paper, pick any $(L, C)$ with that product, and set $G > R$ to sustain. Then press RUN. Match $T$ to within $\pm 4\%$.
stages.concept: The two conditions collapse to one number: $L\,C = (T^{*}/2\pi)^{2}$. Any $(L, C)$ pair with the right product works — that's the pedagogical point of an $\textit{autonomous}$ oscillator: no external drive, one invariant.

labels.peek_hint: count peaks: T* = time between two successive maxima on the target
labels.tip1: move L, C, G — watch envelope decay, sustain, then grow to saturation
labels.tip2: tune L·C so T₀ hits t*, push G above R so the envelope reaches U_sat at t*
labels.tip3: read T* from peak-to-peak, compute L·C = (T*/2π)², set G > R, then RUN

1.1: Start with G = 0: the trace decays because R dissipates every cycle.
1.2: Now push G past R = 10 Ω. The envelope should start growing until it clips at ±4 V.
1.3: Halving L and doubling C keeps L·C the same — same period, but different envelope curvature. Try it.

2.1: The period is T₀ = 2π√(L·C). Compute the target L·C from t* first, THEN pick any (L, C) with that product.
2.2: If the envelope decays instead of saturating, G is too small. Push G above R = 10 Ω.
2.3: Doubling L and halving C keeps T₀ the same. Use this to trade one slider for the other.

3.1: Find two successive positive peaks on the target curve. The time gap between them is T*.
3.2: Compute L·C = (T*/2π)² on paper. Pick any (L, C) pair with that product.
3.3: Then push G above R (= 10 Ω) so the envelope saturates. Press RUN — your curve must overlay the target.
